recipes.name: Chef John’s Easy Homemade Pizza Dough
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups warm water (100 degrees F or 38 degrees C)

steps.text: Stir whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, yeast, salt, sugar, olive oil, and warm water with a spatula until formed into a sticky ball of dough that pulls away from sides of a large bowl, about 3-4 minutes.
Cover the bowl with a light cloth or plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) for 18 hours, until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 550 degrees F (280 degrees C). Sprinkle a baking sheet with cornmeal.

Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and sprinkle with more flour. Form the dough into a rectangle, and cut it into four equal parts. Shape each piece into a ball, stretching and tucking the dough to create a smooth surface, adding more flour if needed. Cover the dough balls with a towel and let rest for 15 minutes.
To shape the dough, sprinkle the surface with flour and lightly pat flat. Use a rolling pin to form a thin disk about 9 inches in diameter.

Transfer the formed crust to the prepared baking sheet and top as desired. Bake on the bottom rack for 4 minutes, move to the middle rack and bake for 5-6 minutes more minutes, until the bottom is crispy and the top is lightly browned. Move to cooling rack to cool slightly before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Easy Homemade Pizza Dough
raw_recipe.description: This pizza dough produces a very nice pizza crust — flavorful, and tender, with just the right amount of chewiness.

review.reviewBody: okay, I just watched the video of chef john making this but I swear he just used 16oz of flour to make 4 pizzas. This calls for 4 cups or 32 oz of flour and says it makes 4 pizzas so I'm confused. I will make it tomorrow then come back and update my review after I figure out what the hey is going on.

The following are the changes I made to perfect this recipe - I used 1/4 cup of wheat flour & 3 3/4 cups of all-purpose flour (instead of 3 cups as recipe states). I let rise as instructed but instead of 18 hours (as recipe states), I covered it with saran wrap & let rise in my oven with the light on for 6 hours (turning every couple hours to make sure both sides of bowl got ample heat). The first time I made this recipe I let rise for 18 hours (covered & placed in oven with light on) & it smelled foul...lol. I put the extra 3 balls of dough in the refrigerator & made a fresh pizza with the last one. When I cooked this pizza I cooked on the bottom rack for 8 minutes & then moved it up one rack for the last 10-13 minutes on 500 degrees since my oven wouldn't heat past 500...lol. Other than these changes I followed the directions as stated. The second time around I was successful with these changes. I hope this helps someone!

Absolutely the best!!! The only things i changed was i added just a pinch more salt, it makes it so flavorful! Then i just used regular flour at 3 1/2 cups. Second time making it and it took less than five minutes to whip it up before letting it sit for an hour. NO NEED to mix the water and yeast separately. Mix all the dry ingredients then the oil and warm water. I didnt make three seperate pizzas i made one rectangle pizza. Once you roll out your shape of your pizza, use a fork to poke holes in it. Bake for about five minutes, THEN put your toppings on it and continue to bake. Nice and fluffy crust, better than pizza restaurants!!!
*i let it sit for hour instead of eighteen.

Best pizza dough ever! We've been using it for years, and I've had many people ask for the recipe. I generally double the yeast and sugar... and it definitely works if it only rises a few hours (though over night is really good). My kids think we should start a restaurant when we use it in the outdoor pizza oven - it's that good! It is very wet to work with, but I work it into round crusts on a well floured surface, and this is perfect. We usually do it indoors on a pizza steel in the oven, and I often pre-bake it slightly before adding toppings, then just broil till it's done.

For all the reviews commenting on the long rise time this is similar to the no-knead "miracle bread" recipe. The long rise contributes to the taste and allows a wonderful flavor to develop, while avoiding kneading. Love this recipe and you can use after a one hour rise.

I have tried so many pizza crusts and never a 5 star!! This is by far the best pizza crust!! I didn't use wheat flour just added added another 1/4 cup of reg. flour!! I also used fast rising yeast!! 18 hours is way too long for me!! Within 4-5 hours dough doubled and was amazing!!! Will never use anothe recipe for crust

This pizza dough was a great recipe. I did make some changes based on what I had. I used 2.5-3 cups all purpose flour and 1 cup break flour. I also used the 1 pkg of rapid rise yeast that was in my pantry. Basically dumped all the ingredients in a bowl except the water mix together add water. Put in own in an oiled bowl to rise. One rise and punch it down. Then cut into 4 pieces. Let it do a 2nd rise. Then just make pizza and bake 400 for 15 mins. Pizza was good now going into food coma.

I use all the same ingredients, but I make it much less complicated.I just mix the wet and dry ingredients separately, then mix.I roll it out and add a little flour as needed to roll it then bake at 400 for 20 mins.Simple!

This dough is pretty good but it really needs more like 3 1/2 cups flour. If you watch the video Chef John weighs the flour - 16 oz - which equates to closer to 3 1/2 cups rather than 3 cups. I made the dough the night before - let it sit until the next afternoon - I made pizza for the kids when they came home from school. They love pizza and this was no exception.
Yes brushed olive oil and sprinkled some Nature's season on crust just before toppings ??
I let it rise for 6-7 hours only...soooo delicious!!!
Super easy and delicious. Thank you Chef John!
Didn’t work fo me. Really wet. Needed way over the asked for recipe. Oh well.
Used this dough a couple times, it's versatile and very forgiving.
We loved it! It became our Sunday dinner and everyone loved it! Making this recipe often!
Love this quick recipe for pizza dough!
The recipe was enough for 3 personalized pizza. Family raved about it.

I followed the directions exactly and it turned out as a gooey sticky mess. I had covered the bowl with plastic wrap and had it in the oven and overnight it formed this odd crust on top. Trying to salvage the dough, I removed the top layer to reveal what looked like sponge so I tried to turn it out to form into a ball but it was too wet and sticky and I had to throw the whole mess away. If I try this again, I will bloom the yeast first rather than add it in dry since it’s not instant yeast

This is really a very good pizza crust. I am used to yeast breads that are kneaded, and so wasn't expecting how soft the dough was after raising. I added probably another cup flour to it. For a bit of flavor I added italian seasoning. The end result was a great pizza. Thank you.

I don't think I've EVER been so profoundly disappointed by a recipe before. Chef John's stuff is usually pretty good, but this came out as a gooey, sticky, unworkable mess. I managed, with some effort, to get it mostly scraped off the pastry mat and into the garbage. 

There's a reason most pizza dough recipes call for kneading. Now I have utterly graphic proof of why that's so. Yecch!
